manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_dual_cable_symmetric_kelvin_deadlock'. At the end of each round: if failing_reasons contains Kelvin unconnected-ratline entries for ALL of /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI, and /SENSEC2_LO simultaneously (both cable pairs in full symmetric failure), increment the counter; otherwise reset it to 0. When the counter reaches 2: (1) for the immediately following round, restrict the compiler's candidate pool exclusively to the four failing Kelvin net members (/SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI, /SENSEC2_LO), zeroing the priority scores of ALL other nets including non-Kelvin unconnected nets such as /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA — these nets must not consume stub slots while both Kelvin gates are simultaneously blocked; (2) issue ripup directives for all four Kelvin net members and any non-Kelvin net whose most recent routed segment passes within 2.5 mm of either shunt pad cluster bounding box; (3) force-inject symmetric Kelvin stub pairs for both cables simultaneously using mandatory_kelvin_bypass, bypassing compiler, absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal for these four stubs; (4) disable the absorber and spur-trimmer for all stubs produced by the restricted compiler in this round so the four Kelvin stubs reach FR unfiltered; (5) log 'dual_cable_symmetric_kelvin_deadlock_exclusive_routing' with fields: (a) round number, (b) counter value, (c) the four Kelvin nets force-injected, (d) the non-Kelvin nets whose priority was zeroed, (e) the nets ripped from shunt proximity; (6) reset the counter to 0 immediately after this bypass round is dispatched. Rationale: Rule 6 handles the mixed state (one symmetric cable plus one asymmetric cable) with immediate first-occurrence ripup, but explicitly requires asymmetry in at least one cable — it does not fire when both cables are simultaneously in full symmetric failure. Rules 33 and 34 force-inject Kelvin stubs per cable but do not zero non-Kelvin competitor nets, so /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA continue draining stub slots each round. During dual-cable symmetric deadlock every compiler stub slot consumed by a non-gate-critical net is a direct opportunity cost against the only path to kelvin_ok=True; the 2-round threshold (rather than Rule 6's immediate first-occurrence) accounts for possible transient dual failure that self-resolves in one round. This rule is additive to Rules 3, 6, 33, 34, 40, 41, and 42; it does not alter net_absorption_count, does not modify compiler_excluded_nets persistently, and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate.
